2 AND XXIII ASCJ, MACT, BENGALURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Nagaraja.M, learned counsel for the appellant in both the appeals as well as Sri.Mallikarjuna Reddy who represents Sri.B.Pradeep, learned counsel on record for respondent No.1 in both the appeals. 
2. While MFA No.2358/2021 is filed challenging the order that is rendered in M.V.C.
No.2604/2019, MFA No.2357/2021 is filed challenging the order that is rendered in M.V.C.
No.2605/2019. Both these orders were rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru on 12.01.2021. 
3. The tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.3,28,600/- to the claimant in M.V.C. No.2604/2019. It awarded a sum of Rs.3,55,000/- to the claimant in M.V.C. No.2605/2019. Being NC:
2024:KHC:47379 dissatisfied with the sum awarded, the respective claimants are before this Court as appellants. 
4. The common facts in both the cases are as under:-
i. Both the appellants sustained injuries in the course of same accident that occurred on 24.02.2019. ii. Both the appellants were working as Fire and Safety Technicians at Fire Track System and Services. iii. PW-4 gave evidence to the effect that both the appellants were drawing consolidated salary of Rs.10,000/- per month. 
Arguments advanced in MFA No.2358/2021 which is connected to M.V.C.
No.2604/2019 and the findings of this Court.
5. Sri. Nagaraja.M, learned counsel for the appellants contends that the appellant sustained grievous injury due to the accident and due to the injury sustained he lost his job. Though sufficient proof was produced to establish the occupation and earnings, the aspect of disability etc, the tribunal awarded meager sum as compensation and therefore this appeal is filed. 
NC: 2024:KHC:47379 6. Contradicting the submission thus made, Sri.Mallikarjuna Reddy, learned counsel for respondent Sri Tushar Shekhar Chougala vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co Ltd on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189963433/ 
3 No.1 submits that the tribunal awarded huge sum as compensation under all heads. Learned counsel further states that no evidence whatsoever is produced to show that the appellant left his job and thereby lost his earnings. Learned counsel also submits that as exorbitant sum is awarded as compensation the appeal is not maintainable. 
7. A perusal of record reveals that the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.3,28,600/- as compensation divided under following heads:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and suffering 30,000-00 Medical expenses 32,556-00 Age, Loss of future income 2,16,000-00 Loss of income during laid up 10,000-00 period Loss of future amenities and 20,000-00 happiness Attendant, conveyance, food 20,000-00 and nourishment charges  Total 3,28,556-00  Rounded of to 3,28,600-00 8. Undisputedly, the appellant sustained fracture of femur right which is grievous in nature. Though the appellant projected that he was earning Rs.14,000/- per month, the NC: 2024:KHC:47379 evidence produced by himself goes to show that he was drawing consolidated pay of Rs.10,000/- per month. Therefore this Court does not find any grounds to interfere with the findings given by the tribunal, that the monthly income of the appellant is required to be considered as Rs.10,000/- per month. 
9. It is not in dispute that the appellant underwent surgery during the course of treatment. Though PW-3 stated that the disability in respect of particular limb is 48% and in respect of whole body is 16%, the tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 10%. The assessment made by the tribunal is valid. Therefore no interference in that regard is required. 
10. By all the evidence that is brought on record the appellant succeed in establishing that he took treatment as inpatient from 24.02.2019 to 08.03.2019.
11. Having considered the nature of injuries sustained, the surgery underwent and the treatment taken, this Court is of the view that the appellant would not have attended his normal pursuits atleast for a period of 3 months. However, the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- only under the head 'loss of NC: 2024:KHC:47379 earning during laid up period'. Also the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- only under the head 'pain and suffering'. However having considered the nature of injuries sustained and the treatment taken and also the disability with which the appellant is left with, this Court is of the view that such sum is disproportionate to the injury sustained. 
Sri Tushar Shekhar Chougala vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co Ltd on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189963433/
4 12. Having considered these aspects, this Court is of the view that globally a sum of Rs.75,000/- is required to be awarded in addition to the sum that is awarded by the tribunal to make the compensation which the appellant would get, justifiable. 
13. Therefore this Court holds that the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.75,000/-in addition to the sum that is awarded by the tribunal.
Arguments advanced in MFA No.2357/2021 which is connected to M.V.C. No.2605/2019 and the findings of this Court.
14. The appellant in this case has sustained right distal radius fracture and underwent surgery for the said injury as per the material available on record. PW -3 assessed the disability in respect of upper limb as 38% and in respect of whole body NC: 2024:KHC:47379 as 12.66%. However,
considering the totality of evidence that is brought on record, the tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 8% which is justifiable. Through the evidence produced, the appellant established that he incurred a sum of Rs.1,12,135/- for treatment and the tribunal indeed awarded the said amount. Sofaras loss of income during laid up period is concerned, the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- only under the said head. However having considered the nature of injuries sustained, this Court is of the view that the appellant would have taken bed rest atleast for a period of 3 months. Also the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- only under the head pain and suffering. As rightly submitted by learned counsel for the appellant such amount is grossly low. The tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.3,55,000/- as compensation divided under following heads:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and suffering 20,000-00 Medical expenses 1,12,135-00 Age, Loss of future income 1,72,800-00 Loss of income during laid up 10,000-00 period Loss of future amenities and 20,000-00 happiness Attendant, conveyance, food 20,000-00 and nourishment charges  Total 3,54,935-00  Rounded of to 3,55,000-00  NC: 2024:KHC:47379 15. As earlier discussed, the compensation granted under the head 'pain and suffering' and 'loss of income during laid up period' is grossly low. Undoubtedly the appellant took treatment as in patient from 24.02.2019 to 28.03.2019. Having considered the period of treatment taken, the nature of Sri Tushar Shekhar Chougala vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co Ltd on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189963433/
5 injuries sustained and the disability with which the appellant is left with and in the light of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the view that the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.70,000/-
in excess to the sum that is awarded by the tribunal. 
16. Thus, both the appeals are disposed of with the following:-
ORDER i. Both the appeals are allowed in part. ii. The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru through orders in M.V.C.
No.2604/2019 dated 12.01.2021 is enhanced by Rs.75,000/-. 
iii. The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru through orders in M.V.C.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:47379 No.2605/2019 dated 12.01.2021 is enhanced by Rs.70,000/-. 
iv. The enhanced sum in both the appeals shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of respective petitions till the date of deposit. v.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire enhanced sum in both the appeals within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order. vi. On deposit, the appellants are permitted to withdraw the entire amount. 
Sd/-
